header:
Date: 2026-09-04
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 68 minutes
Attendees: Alice (Redwood AE), Ben (Redwood SE), Tara (CSM), Jordan (Peregrine Legal), Priya (Procurement), Ethan (Infra), Laila (Security), Samir (Finance)
summary: Workshop to surface MSA/DPA variance items, clarify approval path through Peregrine's governance, align on SLA expectations (latency/TAT for support), and confirm next steps for pricing and private deployment preflight. Several open DPA exceptions and a request for a scoped pilot (1 month) were discussed.
transcript:
[00:00] Alice (AE): Hey everyone good afternoon, thanks for carving out time. We'll run through the MSA redlines, surface the DPA items Jordan flagged, and map the approval path. I'm Alice from Redwood.
[00:15] Jordan (Legal): Hi, Jordan here. Quick note — our procurement team loops in legal for any encryption or data residency stuff early.
[00:22] Priya (Procurement): Yeah, hi. We have a committee threshold at $250k ARR so we need explicit pricing approval and an escalation to finance for anything beyond that.
[00:30] Ben (SE): Great context. On the infra side we'll share the private deployment topology; Redwood Private supports VPC peering or a managed VPC, and we also do customer-managed KMS.
[00:42] Ethan (Infra): When you say managed VPC, is that egress through Redwood egress IPs or can we NAT through our own gateway?
[00:48] Ben (SE): You can do either, we typically support customer egress via NAT, but some enterprises prefer dedicated egress IPs from our side for allowlist simplicity. There may be a small additional fee for static egress.
[01:05] Laila (Security): On KMS, our policy requires that we retain control of keys; we only permit external KMS where CMKs never leave our account. Can Redwood support a bring-your-own-key model with HSM-backed KMS?
[01:16] Ben (SE): Yes, BYOK is supported. For on-prem or VPC we can integrate with AWS KMS/HSM or Azure Key Vault; we'll need a little ops coordination for rotation windows.
[01:31] Jordan (Legal): Back to the DPA — the security questionnaire flagged: data deletion at rest, subprocessor list, and audit log access. We requested that audit logs be exported to our SIEM with at least 90 days retention.
[01:44] Alice (AE): We can do audit exports to your SIEM; retention is configurable but exports are possible. I'll include the log export runbook in the follow-up.
[01:51] Samir (Finance): On pricing — your quote shows committed Dedicated capacity at X GPUs for 12 months. If we push for a lower committed term we need an adjusted price; we also want clarity on overage billing.
[02:05] Alice (AE): Understood. Typical approach: pilot (1 month) on metered hosted, then evaluate Dedicated commit. We can provide a pro forma for a 6-month pilot to mitigate procurement thresholds.
[02:18] Priya (Procurement): The issue is our governance requires an approval matrix — procurement, legal, infra, and SOC/compliance sign-off. Jordan, Laila, you'll need to sign.
[02:29] Jordan (Legal): Correct. Also we have an internal variance policy. If Redwood cannot accept a particular MSA clause, we'll escalate to the contract exceptions committee which meets weekly.
[02:40] Ben (SE): Can you give an example of clauses that typically trigger escalation?
[02:44] Jordan (Legal): Limitations of liability and data processing specifics — for instance, some vendors want to keep subprocessor lists flexible and we push back. Also indemnity carve-outs and audit windows.
[02:56] Alice (AE): On subprocessor transparency, Redwood provides a maintained list and will notify customers 30 days in advance for major changes. We can surface that in the DPA.
[03:10] Laila (Security): 30 days is fine, but we need to ensure high-risk subprocessors get pre-approval.
[03:17] Ben (SE): That's reasonable. For high-risk subprocessors we can add an approval flow.
[03:23] Jordan (Legal): There's also a question of breach notification timelines — our policy is 72 hours. Can Redwood commit to that in the DPA?
[03:31] Alice (AE): We have a 72-hour disclosure practice for material incidents and will include the SOC2 timeline in the security addendum.
[03:38] Priya (Procurement): On SLAs — latency targets are important. Our application has tail-latency SLAs, 95th percentile under 350ms for single-turn responses. How do you benchmark that?
[03:50] Ben (SE): That depends on model, prompt length, and batching. For our hosted small models we can hit 95p < 200ms in many cases, for larger LLMs 95p is higher. For Dedicated we can tune batch sizes and KV cache to meet tighter SLOs. We'll attach benchmark runs from a similar workload.
[04:08] Ethan (Infra): If we do private deployment, what service level for latency do we get in contract vs. a best-effort?
[04:15] Ben (SE): For Dedicated we put SLOs in contract with credits for sustained miss. For private deployments we generally offer operational SLOs plus an add-on for strict p95 latency windows if you buy priority lanes.
[04:30] Samir (Finance): We need to quantify the cost of priority lanes. Also how do the penalties map to refund percentages?
[04:36] Alice (AE): Standard is service credit tiers: for example, p95 miss for more than X minutes triggers Y% credit. We'll add a sample SLA table showing the credit tiers.
[04:46] Jordan (Legal): Another variance is data residency — we need EU-only processing for a subset of data. Can Redwood pin model endpoints to EU regions?
[04:55] Ben (SE): Yes, regional pinning is supported; we can route EU traffic to EU-hosted model instances and keep KV cache regionally isolated.
[05:05] Priya (Procurement): For procurement path clarity: if we have minor MSA redlines, is AE allowed to sign? Or must it go to contract exceptions?
[05:15] Jordan (Legal): Minor redlines under our exception threshold can be handled by procurement with counsel sign-off; anything that materially changes liability goes to committee.
[05:25] Alice (AE): So practical next step — I will send a redlined MSA with the items we discussed marked, and a DPA summary calling out subprocessor, breach notice, and log export options.
[05:34] Tara (CSM): I'll also include an onboarding checklist and a draft pilot statement of work (SOW) so infra can spin up a POC.
[05:41] Ethan (Infra): For the POC we'll need a private VPC peering diagram, expected outbound egress, and a list of firewall IP ranges.
[05:50] Ben (SE): We'll provide the network diagram and the list. Note: static egress IPs may require an additional allocation.
[06:00] Laila (Security): One more thing — auditability. We need to run a one-off audit in the pilot window. Is that acceptable?
[06:07] Alice (AE): Yes, one-off vendor audit requests during pilot are fine; we'll coordinate scope and duration.
[06:14] Samir (Finance): To close the loop on pricing, we'll want a capped estimate for pilot spend so finance can approve.
[06:21] Alice (AE): We'll provide a capped pilot estimate and a path to committed pricing.
[06:28] Jordan (Legal): Please also confirm escrow or data return/rotation mechanics in the MSA. We need assurances for orderly termination.
[06:36] Ben (SE): MSA will include data return options and an export runbook. We'll call out object retention and deletion APIs.
[06:42] Priya (Procurement): Great. Timeline-wise, procurement needs final terms in two weeks to make the next committee meting.
[06:50] Alice (AE): Understood — I'll aim to get materials to you within 4 business days.
[06:55] Jordan (Legal): One small transcription note — we saw a previous vendor call where 'KV cache' got transcribed as 'K V cash' — just flagging for clarity in docs.
[07:03] Ben (SE): haha, happens all the time. We'll ensure acronyms are expanded in the follow-up doc.
[07:10] Tara (CSM): I'll log the decisions: pilot scope, redline MSA, DPA exceptions list, audit export, BYOK, region pinning.
[07:18] Alice (AE): Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the redline package and the network diagrams. Any other blockers?
[07:24] Priya (Procurement): Not from procurement.
[07:27] Laila (Security): No blockers.
[07:29] Jordan (Legal): None. We'll review the redline and get back.
[07:33] Alice (AE): Great. We'll book a pricing alignment session for the week of Sep 14. Thanks all.
[07:38] [call end]
